newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao charged over forgery case, adds to woes.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao charged over forgery case, adds to woes.

text.p: Indian federal police filed criminal charges on Thursday against former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, adding to the political leader's mounting legal troubles, authorities said.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said the charges against Rao and three others related to a 1989 case in which documents were said to have been forged to tarnish the reputation of V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.
The forgery case involved the falsification of bank documents to show that V.P. Singh's son, Ajeya Singh, had a secret bank account with large amounts of money in the Caribbean island of St Kitts.
The criminal charges were believed to be the first against Rao, who is under investigation in at least two other cases but had not been indicted.
The CBI announcement came only hours after a court rejected Rao's request for legal protection against arrest in another criminal case.

The twin legal blows came five days after Rao quit as head of the Congress party. He stepped down in disgrace on Saturday after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court next Monday as a co-accused in a criminal conspiracy case.
But Rao still remains head of Congress's parliamentary party, which includes all Congress law makers.
At the time of the alleged forgery case, V.P. Singh was leading an anti-corruption campaign against the government, having left the ruling Congress party for the opposition.
Singh was appointed prime minister at the end of 1989 after Congress lost general elections.
Authorities later cleared Ajeya Singh of allegations that he had violated foreign exchange and anti-corruption laws.

The federal police agency said the Rao and the other three accused were charged with criminal conspiracy, forgery, giving false evidence and using forged documents. It did not say what possible penalties the charges carried.
The Press Trust of India on Thursday quoted Congress spokesman Devendra Dwivedi as saying that the cases against Rao were a setback to him personally and to the Congress.
Rao could not be reached for comment.

Earlier on Thursday, the Delhi High Court denied Rao's request for anticipatory bail in a $100,000 case of alleged conspiracy to cheat, court officials said. Anticipatory bail protects an accused against arrest.
Rao's lawyer had asked on Wednesday for anticipatory bail before a hearing next Monday in the cheating case.

A source close to Rao's legal team told Reuters late on Thursday that, following the fresh charges in the forgery case, Rao had dropped plans to challenge the denial of interim protection against arrest in India's highest court.
"We will face it in the trial court," the source said.
A strategy to deal with the forgery charges will only be formulated after the court takes up the charges next Tuesday, the source said.
Indian expatriate businessman Lakhubhai Pathak alleges that Rao and a Hindu guru conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983.

Pathak says he paid the money to guru Chandraswami in an unsuccessful attempt to win a state newsprint contract after Rao, then foreign minister, assured Pathak at a meeting in a New York hotel that his "work would be done".
Rao has said he is innocent. He has denied that he was in New York on the dates mentioned by Pathak.
